habitat: Singly in forest fringes and adjacent thickets, riverine forest and well-wooded valleys. It is especially common in coastal bush.
summary: A common resident. Heard more often than seen. The southern morph is plain olive-green. The northern morph, in the lower Zambezi valley and beyond, is much yellower, greener above and yellow-green below. Newman does not say which morph occurs in Kruger. The eyes are creamy-white in adults of both morphs and greyish in immatures. The usual call is a strident Willie!, followed in the breeding season by a babbling trill. The Kemp paper name Sombre Bulbul and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Yellow-bellied Greenbul has bright yellow underparts, including the underwings, and reddish eyes with white eyelids. Sombre Greenbul is the plainer olive bird with a creamy-white eye.

head.pattern: Adult eyes are creamy-white. The identification line also says whitish eyes.

upperparts.pattern: Southern morph: plain olive-green. Northern morph: greener above and much yellower below. Newman does not assign a morph to Kruger.

underparts.pattern: Northern morph is yellow-green below. The southern morph is plain olive-green.

viewNotes.note: Olive bird with a creamy-white eye. The northern morph is yellower, and Newman does not say which morph is in Kruger.
Plain olive-green in the southern morph. The northern morph is greener above.
A flight pattern was not described.
Greyish eye. Newman does not describe the rest of the immature plumage.

calls.description: A strident Willie!. In the breeding season it is followed by a babbling trill. In southern coastal bush the call is often shortened to peeeit, and when agitated it becomes a rapid peeet peeet peeet. Grade A call from Kruger near Skukuza. The filename records a 1 kHz high-pass. research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The yellower morph is assigned to the lower Zambezi and beyond, and Newman does not name the Kruger morph, so no single underpart colour is stored. The grade A call is from Kruger near Skukuza. Its filename records a 1 kHz high-pass, and this site has not filtered it further. No flight photograph was found. Population figures and the Kemp name Sombre Bulbul were left unchanged.
